examples.en: Coins are rolling around on the floor.

examples.ko: 방 안에 빈 병이 굴러다니고 있어요.
examples.en: Empty bottles are lying around in the room.

examples.ko: 공이 방 안을 굴러다니는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear a ball rolling around the room.

examples.ko: 집에 쓰지 않는 물건이 굴러다녀서 정리했어요.
examples.en: Unused things were lying around the house, so I tidied up.

examples.ko: 책상 밑에서 연필이 굴러다니는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a pencil rolling around under the desk.

examples.ko: 이 정도 돈은 길에 굴러다니지 않아요.
examples.en: This much money isn't just lying around on the street.

explain: '굴러가다'는 한 방향으로 가는 것이고, '굴러다니다'는 여기저기로 구르는 것이에요. 물건이 아무 데나 놓여 있을 때도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I tidied up the things lying around in my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '굴러다니다'에 '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form that describes the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The ball kept rolling around on the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지난 일을 말하는 해요체 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form for something that already happened.

phrases.en: Put the pencils in a box so they don't roll around.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 아무 데나 놓이지 않도록 부탁하거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask that things not be left lying around.
phrases.en_equiv: so that it doesn't roll around

explain_en: '굴러가다' rolls in one direction, while '굴러다니다' rolls here and there. It is also commonly used when things are lying about carelessly.

examples.en: The players ran out onto the field.
Children kick a ball on the field.
It rained, so the field got wet.
The field was full of players.

examples.ko: 은퇴하는 선수가 그라운드를 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: The retiring player made one lap around the field.
Fans are happy when the team wins on its home ground.

explain: 학교의 넓은 마당은 '운동장'이라고 하고, 그라운드는 야구나 축구 경기 기사에서 자주 보여요. 자기 팀이 쓰는 경기장은 '홈 그라운드'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Our team won on its home ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 팀이 주로 쓰는 경기장을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The field that a team mainly uses as its own.

phrases.en: The children run and play in the schoolyard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 동네의 넓은 마당은 '그라운드'보다 '운동장'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a wide school or neighborhood yard, 운동장 is used rather than 그라운드.

phrases.en: That player stood on the field for the first time in a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기에 나와서 뛴다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news to mean a player takes the field to play.

explain_en: A school's wide yard is a '운동장', while 그라운드 often appears in reports about baseball or soccer games. A team's own stadium is its '홈 그라운드'.

examples.en: I walked along the river alone on a moonlit night.

examples.ko: 달밤이 너무 밝아서 불을 켜지 않아도 됐어요.
examples.en: The moonlit night was so bright that I didn't need a light.
That night was a moonlit one with a full moon.
A moonlit night in the countryside is quiet and beautiful.
Caught up in the moonlit mood, I hummed a song.
Taking a walk on a moonlit night calms my mind.

explain: 시나 노래, 이야기에서 분위기를 낼 때 자주 나오는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '달이 밝은 밤'이라고 풀어서 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.

phrases.example: 달이 밝은 밤에는 별이 잘 안 보여요.
phrases.en: On a night when the moon is bright, it's hard to see the stars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 이렇게 풀어서 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation people often say it this way.
phrases.en_equiv: a night with a bright moon

phrases.en: I walked in the park with a friend on a moonlit night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 그 밤에 있었던 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에 says what happened on that night.

phrases.en: The moonlit walk was so nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분위기 있는 밤 산책을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a pleasant, atmospheric night walk.

explain_en: It often appears in poems, songs and stories to set a mood. In everyday talk people more often say '달이 밝은 밤' instead.

en: to escape; to make off; to flee

examples.en: The criminal abandoned the car and fled.

examples.ko: 도둑이 담을 넘어 도망하는 모습이 카메라에 찍혔어요.
examples.en: The camera caught the thief climbing over the wall and fleeing.
Don't run away from difficult things.
The teacher found the student who had run off and hidden.
I saw news that the escaped animal had been found.
They say that person fled abroad.

explain: '도망가다', '도망치다', '달아나다'와 뜻이 비슷해요. '일에서 도망하다'처럼 어려운 일이나 책임을 피할 때도 써요. 벗어나려는 곳에는 '에서'를 붙여요.

phrases.en: The cat ran away out the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '도망하다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '도망하다' and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: I was scared, so I just ran away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급하게 벗어나려고 달아나는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger sense of hurrying to get away.

phrases.en: Don't run away from difficult things.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 마세요'를 붙여 피하지 말라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-지 마세요' it tells someone not to avoid something.

explain_en: It is similar in meaning to '도망가다', '도망치다', and '달아나다'. It is also used for dodging hard work or responsibility, as in '일에서 도망하다'. The place you get away from takes '에서'.

p.n: Same meaning; 도망치다 is the more common spoken word.

examples.ko: 청소기를 돌린 뒤에 물걸레로 바닥을 닦아요.
examples.en: After running the vacuum, I wipe the floor with a wet cloth.

examples.ko: 물걸레는 쓰고 나서 꼭 빨아서 널어요.
examples.en: After using the wet cloth, I always wash it and hang it to dry.
My child spilled milk, so I brought a wet cloth.
After mopping with a wet cloth too, the house got really clean.

examples.ko: 로봇 청소기에 물걸레 기능이 있어서 편해요.
examples.en: My robot vacuum has a wet-mop function, so it's convenient.

examples.ko: 창틀은 물걸레보다 마른걸레가 더 잘 닦여요.
examples.en: Window frames get cleaner with a dry cloth than with a wet one.

explain: 반대말은 '마른걸레'예요. 물걸레로 닦는 일은 '물걸레질'이라고 하고, 긴 자루가 달린 것은 보통 '대걸레'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I mop the floor with a wet cloth after vacuuming.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물걸레'로 닦는 일을 말하고, '물걸레질을 하다'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the act of wiping with a wet cloth, used as '물걸레질을 하다'.

phrases.en: If you wipe the floor with a wet cloth, it gets clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물걸레를 도구로 써서 닦는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you wipe something using a wet floorcloth.
phrases.en_equiv: to wipe with a wet cloth

phrases.en: When I finish cleaning, I wash the wet cloth well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소가 끝난 뒤 물걸레를 씻는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for washing the cloth after cleaning.

explain_en: Its opposite is '마른걸레' (dry cloth). Wiping with it is '물걸레질', and the kind with a long handle is usually called '대걸레'.

en: to twinkle; to glitter; to shine

examples.en: Starlight flashed in the night sky and then disappeared.
Lightning flashed in the distance.
A flickering light showed me the way.
His eyes lit up and then he smiled.
The camera flash flashed, so I closed my eyes.
A good idea flashed into my mind.

explain: 반짝하다는 빛이 잠깐 나타났다 사라지거나 짧게 빛나는 모습이에요. 계속 빛나는 것은 '반짝이다'나 '빛나다'가 더 자연스러워요. '반짝 떠오르다'처럼 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The stars in the night sky twinkle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 빛나는 모습은 반짝하다보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is more natural than 반짝하다 for continuous shining.

phrases.en: A good idea suddenly popped into my head.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an idea comes to mind suddenly.

phrases.en: The child's eyes sparkled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧게 한 번 빛나는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a brief single flash of light.

explain_en: 반짝하다 describes a light that appears briefly and fades, or flashes for a moment. For continuous shining, '반짝이다' or '빛나다' is more natural. It is also used for an idea that pops up suddenly, as in '반짝 떠오르다'.

examples.en: You can see many stars in the night sky.
The night sky is prettier in the countryside than in the city.
I made a wish while looking at the night sky.
The dark night sky suddenly lit up.

examples.ko: 캠핑장에서 본 밤하늘도 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget the night sky I saw at the campsite either.
I went up the mountain to take photos of the night sky.

explain: '밤'과 '하늘'이 붙어서 한 단어가 됐어요. 별, 달과 함께 '별이 가득한 밤하늘'처럼 쓰고, 낮에는 따로 부르지 않고 그냥 '하늘'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The stars in the night sky are really pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 써서 하늘 위에 있는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '의' links the night sky to what is in it.

phrases.en: I looked at the night sky in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 별이나 달을 구경할 때 쓰는 가장 쉬운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest pairing for stargazing or moon watching.
phrases.en_equiv: to look at the night sky

phrases.en: The moon rose in the clear night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 좋은 밤을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to picture a night with good weather.

explain_en: It joins 밤 and 하늘 into one word. It goes with stars and the moon, as in 별이 가득한 밤하늘, while the daytime sky is just called 하늘.

en: to be cut; to be chopped; to be hacked

examples.en: My finger got cut on paper.
I got cut by a knife and bled.
I didn't know my leg had been cut by the grass.
Be careful not to get cut by the glass.
I cut my chin while shaving and it hurt.

examples.ko: 요리하다가 손이 베이면 먼저 물로 씻으세요.
examples.en: If your hand gets cut while cooking, rinse it with water first.

explain: 날카로운 것에 몸이 상처 날 때 '~에 베이다'라고 해요. 같은 상황에서 가시나 바늘은 '찔리다'를 써요. 칼로 일부러 자르는 것은 '베다' 쪽이라서 '베이다'와 다르게 써요.

phrases.en: I cut my finger while using a knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 몸의 부분을 주어로 넣어서 어디가 베였는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Make the injured body part the subject to say where you got cut.

phrases.en: A paper cut hurts more than you think.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 베이다'로 무엇 때문에 다쳤는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~에 베이다' to say what caused the cut.

phrases.en: Be careful not to get cut by the glass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다치지 않도록 조심하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to warn someone to be careful not to get cut.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to get cut

explain_en: When something sharp wounds your body, you say '~에 베이다'. For thorns or needles, use 찔리다 instead. Cutting something on purpose with a blade is the verb 베다, which differs from 베이다.

examples.ko: 벼룩시장에서 싼값에 책을 여러 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought several books at a cheap price at the flea market.
A flea market is held in the park every weekend.
I put the clothes I don't wear up for sale at the flea market.
There is so much to look at at the flea market.

examples.ko: 친구랑 벼룩시장에 가서 예쁜 그릇을 구경했어요.
examples.en: I went to the flea market with a friend and looked at pretty dishes.
I asked them to lower the price at the flea market.

explain: 중고 물건이나 직접 만든 물건을 싸게 사고파는 시장이에요. 영어를 그대로 써서 '플리마켓'이라고도 많이 말해요. 인터넷으로 중고 물건을 사고파는 것은 보통 '중고 거래'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I bought clothes at a flea market on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벼룩시장'과 같은 뜻인데 영어를 그대로 쓴 말이라 젊은 사람들이 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 벼룩시장, borrowed from English and popular with young people.

phrases.en: I put my unused clothes out at the flea market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 물건을 팔려고 가져갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you bring your own things there to sell.
phrases.en_equiv: to put out for sale at a flea market

phrases.en: I bought a chair through an online secondhand deal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시장에 가지 않고 인터넷으로 중고 물건을 사고팔 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for buying and selling secondhand goods online, not at a market.

explain_en: It is a market where used or handmade goods are bought and sold cheaply. People also often say '플리마켓', borrowing the English term. Buying and selling used items online is usually called '중고 거래'.

examples.en: I made a wish in my heart while watching the shooting star.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 하늘에서 별똥별이 떨어지는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: Last night I saw a shooting star falling from the sky.

examples.ko: 별똥별은 아주 짧은 시간만 보여서 놓치기 쉬워요.
examples.en: A shooting star is visible only for a very short time, so it is easy to miss.

examples.ko: 별똥별이 많이 떨어지는 날에 캠핑을 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to go camping on the day when many shooting stars fall.

examples.ko: 어두운 곳에 가야 별똥별을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see shooting stars only if you go somewhere dark.
I think I just saw a shooting star!

explain: 과학에서는 '유성'이라고 하지만, 일상에서는 '별똥별'이 더 친근하게 들려요. 별똥별을 보면서 소원을 비는 장면에 많이 나와요. 한꺼번에 많이 떨어지는 것은 '유성우'라고 해요.

phrases.en: A shooting star whizzed across the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 스치는 모습을 말할 때 '지나가다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 지나가다 to describe it passing by quickly.

phrases.en: My friends and I tried to find shooting stars in the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 보려고 하늘을 살필 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you search the sky on purpose to see one.

phrases.example: 오늘 밤에 유성을 볼 수 있대요.
phrases.en: I heard we can see a meteor tonight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '별똥별'이 더 친근해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The science and news word; 별똥별 sounds friendlier in daily life.

explain_en: Science uses '유성', but in daily life '별똥별' sounds friendlier. It often appears in scenes where people make a wish on one. Many falling at once is called a '유성우' (meteor shower).

examples.en: I ran through the rain all the way to school.
I waited a long time in the rain without an umbrella.
The city in the rain looks quiet and lonely.

examples.ko: 빗속으로 걸어 나가는 뒷모습이 슬퍼 보였어요.
examples.en: The figure walking out into the rain looked sad.
Even in the rain, people stood in line and waited.

examples.ko: 그는 빗속에 서서 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He stood in the rain and said nothing.

explain: '물속', '꿈속', '마음속'처럼 '-속'이 붙은 말이에요. '빗속을 걷다', '빗속에서 기다리다'처럼 비를 맞는 상황에서 써요. 사이시옷(ㅅ)이 들어가서 '비속'이 아니라 '빗속'이라고 써요.

phrases.en: I walked in the rain without an umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비를 맞으며 걷는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe walking while getting rained on.

phrases.en: The children ran and played in the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비 오는 중에 뛰는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when running while it's raining.

phrases.en: The singer sang even in the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 와도 계속한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something continued even though it was raining.

explain_en: It is built like '물속', '꿈속' and '마음속', with '-속' attached. It is used in situations where you are out in the rain, as in '빗속을 걷다' and '빗속에서 기다리다'. A sound-linking ㅅ is added, so it is written 빗속, not '비속'.

examples.en: The baby gives mom a kiss on the cheek.
The child gave a kiss as a greeting.
If you want to give a kiss, ask first.
My puppy likes giving kisses on my face.
Grandma smiles every time I give her a kiss.
I give my child a kiss before bed.

explain: '키스하다'보다 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이라 아이, 가족, 연인 사이에 써요. 명사 '뽀뽀'를 써서 '뽀뽀를 하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: I give my child a kiss before bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뽀뽀하다'와 뜻이 같고, '를'을 넣으면 말이 조금 또렷해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword; adding the object particle makes it a bit more explicit.

phrases.en: Mom, please give me a kiss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이고, 아이들이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request form that children often use.

phrases.en: Dad kissed the baby on the forehead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뽀뽀하는 몸의 자리를 '에'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spot being kissed is marked with 'e'.

explain_en: It is lighter and cuter than 'kiseuhada', and is used with children, family, and couples. You can also use the noun: 'ppopporeul hada'.

examples.en: My father has run a business in Seoul for a long time.

examples.ko: 저는 대학교를 졸업하고 나서 사업하고 싶어요.
examples.en: After I graduate from university, I want to start my own business.
My friend runs a business in China by himself.
If you run a business, you hardly have any days off.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 십 년 동안 사업했지만 지금은 회사에 다녀요.
examples.en: My uncle ran a business for ten years, but now he works at a company.
I work hard to save money to start a business.

explain: '사업을 하다', '사업을 시작하다'처럼 '사업'에 동사를 붙여 말하는 일도 많아요. 작은 가게에서 물건을 파는 일은 '장사하다'라고 하고, '사업하다'는 회사 단위의 더 큰 일이라는 느낌이에요. 사업하는 사람은 '사업가', 가게나 회사 주인은 '사장님'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: My uncle runs a business in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사업하다'와 뜻이 같고, '사업'을 따로 떼어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 사업하다, with 사업 split out as a noun.

phrases.example: 작년에 작은 회사를 만들어서 사업을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: Last year I set up a small company and started a business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사업을 처음 열 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you first start a business.

phrases.en: My dream is to become a businessperson.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사업하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who does business.

explain_en: People often say '사업을 하다' or '사업을 시작하다' with the noun and a separate verb. Selling goods in a small shop is '장사하다'; '사업하다' feels larger and company-sized. A person who runs a business is a '사업가', and the owner of a shop or company is called '사장님'.

examples.en: A pretty dress is hanging in the shop window.

examples.ko: 지나가다가 쇼윈도 속 구두가 마음에 들었어요.
examples.en: While passing by, I liked the shoes in the shop window.
The shop owner decorated the window display anew.

examples.ko: 쇼윈도 앞에서 아이가 한참 서 있어요.
examples.en: The child has been standing in front of the shop window for a while.
The shop window lights stay on even at night.
I saw the sale notice stuck on the shop window.

explain: '진열대'는 가게 안에도 있지만, 쇼윈도는 밖에서 유리 너머로 구경하는 곳이에요. 보통 '쇼윈도를 구경하다', '쇼윈도에 진열하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 저 부부는 남들 앞에서만 다정한 쇼윈도 부부래요.
phrases.en: a showcase couple
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 좋지 않은데 남들에게는 사이좋은 척하는 부부를 말해요. 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A couple who act happy in public but are not close in private. It sounds a bit sarcastic.
phrases.en_equiv: a couple putting on a show for others

explain_en: A '진열대' (display shelf) can be inside a shop, but a 쇼윈도 is the glass display you look at from outside. It is usually used as '쇼윈도를 구경하다' (to window-shop) or '쇼윈도에 진열하다' (to display in the window).

examples.en: How on earth did you hurt your leg like that?
How did you end up becoming friends with that person?
I hear from him once in a while.
I accidentally deleted the file by mistake.
I happened to run into an old friend on the street.
How did you end up this late today?

explain: 질문에서 '어쩌다가 ~했어요?'라고 하면 어떻게 그런 일이 생겼는지 놀라거나 걱정하며 묻는 말이에요. 평서문에서는 '우연히'나 '가끔'에 가까워서 '어쩌다가 한 번'처럼 써요. 줄여서 '어쩌다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Somehow I ended up coming all the way here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어쩌다가'를 줄여 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 'eojjeodaga'.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 어쩌다가 한 번 연락해요.
phrases.en: That friend contacts me only once in a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가끔 있는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that happens only occasionally.

phrases.en: Your hand looks hurt. How did that happen?
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떻게 그런 일이 생겼는지 놀라거나 걱정하며 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask in surprise or concern how something happened.

explain_en: In a question, '어쩌다가 ~했어요?' asks how something came about, often with surprise or concern. In a statement it is close to 'by chance' or 'occasionally', as in '어쩌다가 한 번' (once in a while). It is often shortened to '어쩌다'.

examples.en: I steep tea in hot water.
Yesterday I made broth by simmering dried anchovies.

examples.ko: 티백을 너무 오래 우리면 쓴맛이 나요.
examples.en: If you steep a tea bag too long, it tastes bitter.
I drank the barley tea my grandmother brewed.
I'm going to cold-brew green tea.
After simmering the beef bones for a long time, the broth turned white.

explain: 차나 국물처럼 재료의 맛과 색을 물에 내는 일에 써요. 재료가 주어가 아니라 목적어예요: '차를 우리다'. 같은 그림에서 재료 쪽을 말하면 '우러나다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I brew barley tea and drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우려'와 '마시다'를 이어서 차를 만들어 마신다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links 우려 and 마시다 to mean making tea and drinking it.

phrases.en: I make broth from anchovies and kelp.
phrases.nuance_ko: '우리다'와 거의 같고, 맛을 뽑아낸다는 느낌이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 우리다, but with a clearer sense of extracting flavor.

phrases.en: Steep the tea bag for about three minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-세요'를 붙여 차를 만드는 방법을 정중하게 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -세요 politely gives instructions for making tea.

explain_en: Used when you draw the flavor and color of an ingredient into water, as with tea or broth. The ingredient is the object: '차를 우리다'. From the ingredient's side, say '우러나다' (the flavor comes out).

examples.en: Please take a toothpick from next to the cashier.

examples.ko: 이쑤시개로 이를 쑤시는 건 보기 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: Picking your teeth with a toothpick doesn't look nice.
We stick the rice cake on a toothpick and eat it.

examples.ko: 이쑤시개가 다 떨어져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: We've run out of toothpicks, so I need to buy new ones.

examples.ko: 이쑤시개 한 통에 몇 개 들었어요?
examples.en: How many are in one box of toothpicks?

examples.ko: 이쑤시개는 입을 가리고 쓰는 게 예의예요.
examples.en: It is polite to cover your mouth when using a toothpick.

explain: 식당 계산대 옆에 놓여 있는 경우가 많아요. 이를 쑤시는 용도 말고도 과일이나 떡을 집어 먹는 데도 써요. '이'(teeth)와 '쑤시다'(poke)가 합쳐진 말이라서 소리 나는 대로 [이쑤시개]라고 해요.

phrases.en: I picked up the fruit with a toothpick and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이를 쑤시는 것 말고 음식을 집을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for picking up food, not just cleaning teeth.

phrases.en: I used a toothpick at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사용한다는 뜻으로 가장 기본적으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you used one.

phrases.en: Please give me just one toothpick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수를 세어 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask for a specific number.

explain_en: It is often left next to the cashier in restaurants. Besides cleaning teeth, it's also used to pick up fruit or rice cakes. It combines '이' (teeth) and '쑤시다' (to poke) and is pronounced [이쑤시개].

en: to cut with a knife; to slice

examples.en: The chef chops quickly on the cutting board.
Don't chop the onion too big.
Even the way that chef handles a knife is different.
I almost cut my hand while chopping vegetables.

examples.ko: 손목에 힘을 빼고 칼질하면 덜 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you relax your wrist when you cut, it is less tiring.

examples.ko: 스테이크를 칼질할 때는 포크로 고기를 잡아요.
examples.en: When you cut a steak, you hold the meat with a fork.

explain: '썰다'는 재료를 자른다는 데 초점이 있고, '칼질하다'는 칼을 쓰는 동작이나 솜씨에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 '칼질이 빠르다', '칼질이 능숙하다'처럼 솜씨를 말할 때도 잘 써요.

phrases.en: It's our anniversary today, so let's go out for a steak dinner!
phrases.nuance_ko: 스테이크나 돈가스처럼 칼로 썰어 먹는 서양식 식사를 하러 간다는 말로, 편한 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In casual talk it means going out for a Western-style meal, such as steak or pork cutlet, that you cut with a knife.
phrases.en_equiv: go out for a steak dinner

explain_en: '썰다' focuses on cutting the ingredient, while '칼질하다' focuses on the action of using the knife and the skill involved. That is why people also say '칼질이 빠르다' (quick with a knife) or '칼질이 능숙하다' (skilled with a knife).

examples.en: This file is made up of text only.
I copied the text and pasted it into Notepad.

examples.ko: 사진 속 텍스트를 읽을 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can you read the text in the photo?

examples.ko: 텍스트가 너무 작아서 글자 크기를 키웠어요.
examples.en: The text was too small, so I enlarged the font size.
In class we read an English text together.
I sent the meeting time in a text message.

explain: 텍스트는 사진이나 소리가 아닌 글자로 된 내용을 말해요. 컴퓨터에서는 '텍스트 파일', '텍스트 입력'처럼 쓰고, 수업에서는 읽고 공부하는 글 자료를 텍스트라고도 해요. 일상에서는 '글'이나 '문자'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I saved this document as a text file.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자만 들어 있는 컴퓨터 파일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A computer file that contains only text.

phrases.en: Please enter the text here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 휴대폰에 글자를 쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when typing words into a computer or phone.

phrases.en: We read a short text in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업에서 공부하는 글 자료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a reading passage studied in class.

explain_en: 텍스트 is content made of written characters rather than images or sound. On computers it appears in '텍스트 파일' and '텍스트 입력', and in class it can mean a written passage you study. In daily talk, '글' or '문자' is more common.

examples.ko: 아침마다 학교 트랙을 열 바퀴 달려요.
examples.en: Every morning I run ten laps around the school track.

examples.ko: 트랙 위에서 선수들이 출발 준비를 해요.
examples.en: The runners get ready to start on the track.

examples.ko: 육상 경기장의 트랙은 한 바퀴가 사백 미터예요.
examples.en: One lap of a stadium track is four hundred meters.

examples.ko: 이 트랙에서는 비 오는 날에 미끄러워요.
examples.en: This track gets slippery on rainy days.

examples.ko: 앨범의 첫 번째 트랙이 가장 좋아요.
examples.en: The first track on the album is the best.

examples.ko: 트랙마다 분위기가 달라서 계속 듣게 돼요.
examples.en: Each track has a different mood, so I keep listening.

explain: 달리기 경기장의 둥근 길을 '트랙'이라고 하고, 음악에서는 앨범 속 곡 하나를 '트랙'이라고 해요. 앨범에서 몇 번째 곡인지는 '1번 트랙'처럼 번호를 붙여 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 매일 트랙을 세 바퀴 돌아요.
phrases.en: I go around the track three times every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동장 트랙에서 달리거나 걸을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for running or walking laps around a track.

phrases.en: On this album, track 1 is the best.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악 앨범에서 곡의 순서를 말할 때 번호를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a number to name a song's place on a music album.

phrases.en: The athletes are running on the track.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기장 트랙을 말할 때 '에서'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '에서' for the running track at a stadium.

explain_en: '트랙' is the oval running lane of a stadium, and in music it means a single song on an album. The song's position is given with a number, as in '1번 트랙' (track 1).

examples.en: My friend yawns loudly during class.
I went to bed late yesterday, so I have been yawning since morning.

examples.ko: 제 동생이 하품하는 모습이 고양이 같아요.
examples.en: The way my younger sibling yawns looks like a cat.

examples.ko: 한 명이 하품하면 다른 사람도 따라 해요.
examples.en: When one person yawns, others do it too.
I was sleepy and teared up while yawning.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 하품할 것 같아서 물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: I felt like yawning during the meeting, so I drank some water.

explain: '하품을 하다'처럼 목적어를 넣어서도 쓰고 '하품하다'로 붙여서도 써요. 한국에서는 사람들 앞에서 하품할 때 손으로 입을 가리는 것이 예의예요.

phrases.en: I'm tired, so I keep yawning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하품하다'를 둘로 나눠 '을'을 넣은 말로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: This splits 하품하다 with '을'; the meaning is the same.

phrases.en: The class is boring, so I can't stop yawning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하려고 한 것이 아니라 저절로 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when a yawn comes out on its own.

phrases.en: I held back a yawn during the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들 앞에서 하품이 나오는 것을 참을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when you hold back a yawn in front of other people.

explain_en: You can say it with an object, '하품을 하다', or as one word, '하품하다'. In Korea it is polite to cover your mouth with your hand when you yawn in front of people.

examples.en: Yesterday I bought books cheaply at a used bookstore.
There is one old used bookstore in my neighborhood.
Every weekend I go browsing at a used bookstore with a friend.
The used bookstore owner recommended a book to me.

examples.ko: 헌책방은 책이 쌓여 있어서 길 찾기가 어려워요.
examples.en: In a used bookstore, books are piled up, so it's hard to find your way.

examples.ko: 졸업한 뒤에도 그 헌책방을 가끔 찾아가요.
examples.en: Even after graduating, I sometimes visit that used bookstore.

explain: 새 책을 파는 '서점'과 달리 이미 읽은 책을 사고파는 가게예요. 가격이 싸고 오래된 책을 만날 수 있어서 구경하러 가는 사람도 많아요.

phrases.en: I go to a used bookstore on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에 가다'를 붙여 가게에 가는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -에 가다 to talk about going to the shop.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to a used bookstore

phrases.en: Seoul has a famous used bookstore street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헌책방이 여러 개 모여 있는 거리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A street where many used bookstores gather.

phrases.en: The used bookstore owner recommended a book to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게를 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the person who runs the shop.

explain_en: Unlike a '서점' that sells new books, this shop buys and sells books that have already been read. Prices are low and you can find old books, so many people go just to browse.

en: to spin; to turn around; to rotate

examples.en: The Earth rotates once a day.
The ride started to spin slowly.
The wheel is spinning very fast.

examples.ko: 이 손잡이는 오른쪽으로 회전하면 소리가 커져요.
examples.en: If you turn this knob to the right, the volume goes up.
The fan blades spin and the air comes out.
Try going in through the revolving door.

explain: 바퀴나 지구처럼 축을 중심으로 도는 것에 써요. 사람이 몸을 돌릴 때는 '돌다'나 '돌아서다'가 자연스러워요. 차가 길에서 방향을 바꾸는 것은 '우회전', '좌회전'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: There is a swivel chair in the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회전'을 다른 말 앞에 붙여서 도는 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '회전' before another noun names something that rotates.

phrases.en: The wheel spins round and round.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌다'는 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '돌다' is the easier word for everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The ride spins round and round.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빙글빙글'을 앞에 붙이면 계속 도는 모습이 더 잘 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '빙글빙글' makes the continuous spinning motion vivid.

explain_en: It is used for things that turn around an axis, like a wheel or the Earth. When a person turns their body, 돌다 or 돌아서다 sounds more natural. A car turning at a corner is called 우회전 or 좌회전.

examples.en: The sky has been clouding over since the afternoon.

examples.ko: 말을 돌려서 하면 뜻이 흐려지기 쉬워요.
examples.en: If you speak in a roundabout way, the meaning easily becomes unclear.

examples.ko: 눈이 나빠서 멀리 있는 글자가 흐려지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My eyesight is bad, so faraway letters seem to blur.

examples.ko: 시간이 지나면 기억이 점점 흐려지게 돼요.
examples.en: As time passes, memories gradually fade.
My vision, which had been hazy like fog, gradually cleared.
If the weather turns cloudy, bring an umbrella.

explain: '날씨가 흐리다'는 지금 상태이고, '흐려지다'는 점점 그렇게 변하는 과정이에요. 날씨뿐 아니라 기억, 시야, 경계가 분명하지 않게 될 때도 쓰고, 반대는 '맑아지다'나 '선명해지다'예요.

phrases.en: The sky suddenly turned cloudy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 점점 나빠질 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most common when the weather is getting worse.

phrases.en: It was long ago, so my memory has faded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기억이 분명하지 않게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a memory becomes unclear.

phrases.en: I'm so tired that my vision gets blurry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 것이 또렷하지 않게 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when what you see becomes unclear.

explain_en: '날씨가 흐리다' is the current state, while '흐려지다' is the process of gradually becoming so. It is used not only for weather but also when memory, vision or boundaries become unclear, and the opposites are '맑아지다' and '선명해지다'.
